flow.name: pm-upload-to-optimization
flow.description: PM user uploads new alpha.pkl and optimization.xlsx files. Portal reads those files to populate the Trade tab with fresh optimization data.

steps.step: PM user opens UploadPortfolioModal in PortfolioManagement Trade tab
Portal calls GET /api/private/portfolio-management/upload-urls?fund={fund}&date={date} (opal-pm-upload-urls Lambda)
Lambda validates fund (PFDE|PFOE|TAX), date (YYYYMMDD), and JWT tier=internal; returns presigned PUT URLs with 15-minute expiry
Portal uses XMLHttpRequest PUT to upload alpha.pkl to opal-data-pm/{fund}/alpha/{date}.pkl
Portal uses XMLHttpRequest PUT to upload optimization.xlsx to opal-data-pm/{fund}/optimization/{date}.xlsx
PM user navigates to the optimization view (or triggers reload)
Portal calls GET /api/private/portfolio-management/load?fund={fund}&date={date} (opal-pm-optimization-loader Lambda)
opal-pm-optimization-loader reads alpha.pkl and optimization.xlsx from opal-data-pm, transforms to optimization response shape, returns 503 securities with 33 factors
Portal populates useOptimizationState with securities, alpha/sector/model/risk data, summary, and optimization dates

flow.note: The task order requirement listed yang-pipeline-trigger, yang-validate-files, yang-ingest-dynamodb, and yang-move-to-processed as steps in this flow. Based on Lambda source code, the PM upload target is opal-data-pm while yang-pipeline-trigger watches opal-data-portal-v2/uploads/manifest.json. These are SEPARATE trigger paths. The yang-pipeline-trigger connection to PM uploads could not be confirmed from source — see gaps section.

flow.name: datarefresh-to-yang-pipeline
flow.description: Dev user triggers full portal data regeneration. Yang pipeline Step Functions executes generate-* Lambdas (owned by DS_PortfolioAnalytics) and ingests market data (owned by DS_MarketIntelligence).

steps.step: Dev user on DataRefresh page uploads PKL, Excel, CSV files via FileDropZone
POST /api/scoped/data-refresh/upload-urls returns { uploadId, presigned PUT URLs per file } (opal-data-refresh-api)
XHR PUTs upload files to opal-data-portal-v2 staging path (uploadId-scoped)
POST /api/scoped/data-refresh/trigger moves files to opal-data-portal-v2/uploads/ and creates manifest.json
S3 event on uploads/manifest.json triggers yang-pipeline-trigger Lambda

yang-pipeline-trigger reads manifest; extracts data_as_of_date from manifest date field (YYYYMMDD -> YYYY-MM-DD); generates pipeline_execution_id (UUID); writes json/yang-pipeline-metadata.json and json/latest/{file_type}.json to opal-data-portal-v2
yang-pipeline-trigger starts YangDataPipeline Step Functions (ARN: arn:aws:states:us-east-1:313476888478:stateMachine:YangDataPipeline); returns 409 if already RUNNING
Step Functions: yang-validate-files verifies all manifest-listed files exist in uploads/ prefix of opal-data-portal-v2; returns manifest + file_metadata
Step Functions: yang-move-to-processed copies PKL files from uploads/ to opal-data-portal-v2/benchmarks/ with canonical naming ({file_type}_{YYYYMMDD}_{version}.pkl)
Step Functions: yang-ingest-dynamodb reads data PKL, ingests market data to opal-portal-market-data DynamoDB table (DAILY#YYYY-MM-DD entries and LATEST entries — used by MarketIntelligence pod)

Step Functions: yang-generate-* Lambdas (DS_PortfolioAnalytics scope) execute positioning, attribution, factor tilts, valuation, macroeconomics, correlation generators — write JSON views to opal-data-portal-v2/json/
Portal polls GET /api/scoped/data-refresh/status/{executionId} every 3s; displays PipelineProgress grouped by step until terminal state
On SUCCEEDED: Portal shows navigation links to Valuation, Market Overview, Model Portfolios pages

flow.name: export-and-submit-to-tradesubmission
flow.description: PM user completes optimization, reviews Trade tab, and triggers Export-and-Submit. This is the primary PM-to-operations handoff — creates a trade submission record that appears in TradeSubmission's Approvals tab for review and execution.

steps.step: PM user reviews Trade tab (503 securities with optimizedWeight and finalTrade columns), confirms override weights and trade instructions
PM user opens ExportModal, selects destination (brokerage), reviews attestation checkboxes, confirms Export and Submit

Portal calls POST /api/private/portfolio/export-and-submit with full ExportAndSubmitRequest (fund, account, destination, weightsAsOf, tradesAsOf, attestations, securities[], initiatorEmail, initiatorName)
Backend Lambda (opal-portfolio-excel-generator inferred) generates Vident Trade CSV from securities data; uploads to S3
Backend creates TradeSubmission DynamoDB record with status PENDING_APPROVAL, submissionId (format: TRADE-{YYYYMMDD}-{HHmmss}-{random}), excel_s3_key pointing to Vident CSV
Response returns { versionId, submissionId, tradeCsvUrl, tradeCsvKey, exportedAt, totalSecurities, tradeCount }
PM History tab displays this version's submissionId as a navigation link to TradeSubmission page

Approver in TradeSubmission: POST /api/general/trades/workflow action=approve (trade-workflow-handler) -> APPROVED
Executor in TradeSubmission: POST /api/general/trades/workflow action=execute -> EXECUTED; sends to brokerage
TradeSubmission: POST /api/general/trades/workflow action=complete -> COMPLETE (auto-triggered or admin action)

flow.name: trade-lifecycle-state-machine
flow.description: Complete trade status progression and rejection paths.

steps.step: PENDING_APPROVAL (created by export-and-submit or manual submit via SubmitTab)
approve action -> APPROVED (appears in Execution tab)
reject action (from PENDING_APPROVAL) -> REJECTED (appears in History tab)
execute action (from APPROVED) -> EXECUTED
reject action (from APPROVED) -> REJECTED
complete action (from EXECUTED) -> COMPLETE (appears in History tab)

flow.note: All transitions via POST /api/general/trades/workflow. rejection_reason required for reject action. All actions require user_email and user_name for audit trail.

dependency.description: All /api/private/* routes require JWT validated by auth-validator-edge. User context (X-User-Email, X-User-Tier) injected as headers. Tier must be 'internal' for PM and portfolio Lambdas. DataRefresh requires userType 'Dev' claim in JWT. data_quality_notes.note: Dual auto-save race condition risk: opal-pm-optimization-autosave-put (full state, 60s) and opal-portfolio-autosave-put (legacy delta, 60s) both run concurrently. If the legacy path reads and merges the existing 505-trade record at the same time the optimization path writes, the result could be partial state. No lock or transaction coordination exists between the two paths based on available source code.

DynamoDB item size risk for snapshots: opal-pm-snapshot-handler stores full securities arrays as JSON strings. A 503-security array with 33 factors each can exceed the 400KB DynamoDB limit. Lambda logs a warning at item_size > 400KB but does not fail the put_item call — the DynamoDB service will return an error if the limit is exceeded. No S3 overflow path exists.

Summary stats are partially stubbed: predictedBeta, totalRisk, assetSelection, and commonFactor in PortfolioSummary are calculated stubs in useOptimizationCalculations.ts (lines 61-64). The UI displays these as 0 or placeholder values. They are saved as-is in auto-saves and snapshots.

AUM is hardcoded at $100M default in usePortfolioEditStore.ts:143. The optimization loader may return aum in the summary, but the edit store does not pull from it. Export and submission summary stats using AUM (turnover cost estimates) will be based on the default.

SEDOL/ISIN/FIGI not populated in transformToExportTrade (portfolio.ts:343-349). The ExportTrade sent to export-and-submit has sedol: undefined, isin: undefined, figi: undefined. These fields are present in TradeSubmission's TradeSecurity type but will be empty on PM-sourced submissions.

yang-pipeline-trigger: if execution age exceeds 600s, Lambda logs an alert but still returns 409 — it does not auto-terminate the stuck execution. Manual intervention (Step Functions console) is required.

TradeSubmission uses publicApiRequest (no JWT scope). Identity relies solely on user_email in request body. No RBAC enforcement at the API gateway level — all business logic enforcement is in the Lambda functions. Approver/executor identity can be set to any email string by the client.

opal-smartx-ingestion-pipeline uses emoji characters in logger.info calls (e.g., "checkmark" character). Per CLAUDE.md rule 13, emojis break CloudWatch log queries on Windows. This is an existing issue in deployed code, not introduced by this analysis.

However, opal-pm-upload-urls writes to opal-data-pm, while yang-pipeline-trigger is triggered by S3 events on opal-data-portal-v2/uploads/manifest.json. These are separate buckets. opal-pm-optimization-loader source (infra/aws/lambda/portfolio_optimization_loader/) was not found locally, so it cannot be confirmed whether it reads from yang pipeline outputs or directly from opal-data-pm. The critical_flow pm-upload-to-optimization documents the upload-and-load path based on what is confirmed. The yang-pipeline-trigger connection is not verified.
